# .Header is not response state muxt has to write: it sets a key on the
# response header map when the template runs. So it works whoever owns the
# response, and a method taking the response argument may still use it.
#
# This is the other side of err_redirect_with_response_argument.txt. The
# diagnostic there has to name only the methods that genuinely cannot work, or
# it breaks routes that were fine.

muxt generate --use-receiver-type=T
grep 'mux\.HandleFunc\("GET /with-response"' template_routes.go

# The method owns the response, so muxt writes no status code for this route.
! grep 'statusCode := cmp\.Or' template_routes.go

exec go build ./...

-- go.mod --
module server

go 1.24
-- template.gohtml --
{{- define "GET /with-response WithResponse(ctx, response)" -}}
	{{- .Header "x-example" "set-from-template" -}}
{{- end -}}
-- template.go --
package server

import (
	"context"
	"embed"
	"html/template"
	"net/http"
)

//go:embed *.gohtml
var templatesFS embed.FS

var templates = template.Must(template.ParseFS(templatesFS, "*"))

type T struct{}

func (T) WithResponse(ctx context.Context, response http.ResponseWriter) any { return nil }
